text.p: Shares in Europe's largest mobile phone maker Nokia Oy rose in active dealings on Friday, fuelled by recent large orders and upbeat comments by the company's CEO in a Swiss newspaper, brokers said.

At 1200/0900 GMT, Nokia was trading up 5.20 markka or just over two percent at 218.00 markka, probing new year-high levels and retracing its steps through levels the stock plunged past late last year after it issued a shock profit warning.
It earlier touched 219.00 markka in releatively active volume totalling around 100 million markka so far.

In a report published on Wednesday, Swiss newspaper Finans und Wirdschaft quoted Nokia CEO Jorma Ollila as saying he expected the company to maintain double-digit sales growth in mobile phones over the next five years, which brokers said was one factor boosting demand.

"We expect that the mobile phone market (growth) will be around 30 percent in the next five years. Nokia will against this background make at least two-digit turnover growth," Ollila said in the interview, a copy of which the company released.
In addition, the market was only now reacting to news earlier this week that Nokia had won a 300 billion lira GSM expansion network order in Italy, brokers said.
